problemStatement.formal: ∃ c₁ c₂ : ℝ, 0 < c₂ ∧ c₂ ≤ c₁ ∧ ∃ N₀, ∀ n > N₀, 6n - c₁·n^{2/3} ≤ f₃(n) < 6n - c₂·n^{2/3}
problemStatement.plain: The maximum number of unit-distance pairs among n separated points in ℝ³ is f₃(n) = 6n - Θ(n^{2/3}). The leading term 6n comes from the kissing number τ(3) = 12, and the correction term n^{2/3} reflects the isoperimetric surface-to-volume ratio.
whyMatters: Connects finite sphere packing theory to the Kepler conjecture
The isoperimetric exponent (d-1)/d unifies 2D (Harborth) and 3D patterns
Understanding f₃(n) precisely reveals the fine structure of FCC/HCP packings

proven: f₂(n) ≤ 3n from τ(2) = 6 (machine-verified from kissing axiom)
f₃(n) ≤ 6n from τ(3) = 12 (machine-verified from kissing axiom)
Isoperimetric exponent (d-1)/d: proved 1/2 for d=2, 2/3 for d=3, monotone in d
open: FCC cluster lower bound: f₃(n) ≥ 6n - c·n^{2/3}
Exact constants in the Θ(n^{2/3}) correction
knownResults.goal: Prove or further formalize the Erdős conjecture f₃(n) = 6n - Θ(n^{2/3})
